narrativeReportMd:
# OrganizationAffiliation R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`OrganizationAffiliation` keeps the same resource identity, but it has a material local contact-model break: R4 `OrganizationAffiliation.telecom` is removed and R6 introduces `OrganizationAffiliation.contact` as `ExtendedContactDetail`. Existing R4 instances that contain `telecom` are not valid R6 instances without transformation, and rich R6 `contact` content cannot be represented losslessly in base R4.

## Scope
The analysis covers the base resource StructureDefinition plus related datatypes and terminology needed to interpret local element changes. Inherited `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, and datatype-wide changes are out of scope for this report. Search parameters are also out of scope, even though the package indexes show OrganizationAffiliation search parameters in both releases.

## Main migration themes
The main migration work is contact data remodeling. R4 repeated `ContactPoint` values should generally become R6 `contact` entries containing `telecom`; however, R6 can also carry contact purpose, name, address, responsible organization, and period. That richer structure creates R6→R4 data-loss risk. R6 also adds local errors forbidding `home` use for contact telecoms and addresses, so simple mechanical mapping of R4 `telecom.use = home` can fail validation.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is `OrganizationAffiliation.telecom` → `OrganizationAffiliation.contact` because it is both a wire-format path change and a type-domain change. A secondary runtime issue is that the old R4 `telecom` element was summary=true, while the replacement R6 `contact` element is summary=false.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for contact migration policies: whether to split or group old telecom repetitions, what to do with `home` contact uses, and whether richer R6 contact details need extensions or an out-of-band preservation strategy when projecting back to R4.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 contact model is probably justified by the need for richer and more reusable official contact details, but a less disruptive transition could have retained `telecom` for one release while adding optional `contact`. The local `home` contact prohibition could also have been introduced as a warning or profile constraint before becoming a base error.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `ExtendedContactDetail`, `Resource`/`DomainResource`, and OrganizationAffiliation search parameters separately for full migration planning.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: The resource identity is stable, but the local contact model is breaking: R4 `telecom` is removed, R6 `contact` uses `ExtendedContactDetail`, and R6 forbids `home` use in OrganizationAffiliation contacts. The largest uncertainty is the absence of an official cross-version map for contact migration.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration centers on contact transformation. R4 `telecom: ContactPoint[]` can usually map to R6 `contact[].telecom[]`, but systems must decide grouping, summary behavior, and how to handle `home` contact uses. R6→R4 projection is lossy for `contact.purpose`, `contact.name`, `contact.address`, `contact.organization`, and `contact.period` unless extensions or external metadata are used. Other local elements preserve cardinality, types, and reference targets.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because both R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions are present and have the same canonical identity. Confidence is medium for migration policy and semantic intent because no official diff, change note, or cross-version ConceptMap/StructureMap was available. Terminology confidence is adequate for packaged compose comparisons, but not for live SNOMED expansion details.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 represents the same business area through `OrganizationAffiliation.contact`, whose `ExtendedContactDetail` value can include purpose, name, telecom, address, organization, and period.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements have the same parent, same optional repeating cardinality, nearly identical requirements text, and both describe contact details at the participating organization. The change is best understood as a replacement/rename plus type-domain expansion rather than an unrelated removal and addition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format break for R4→R6: an R4 instance containing `OrganizationAffiliation.telecom` uses an element that is absent from the R6 resource definition. Strict R6 parsers and validators will reject the unknown element unless a transform rewrites it to `contact`. It is also a high R6→R4 risk because valid R6 `ExtendedContactDetail` content can contain purpose, name, address, responsible organization, and period that have no native R4 `OrganizationAffiliation.telecom` representation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Organization affiliation contact details may drive operational routing, contracting, provider-directory support, or service-access workflows. Dropping or flattening them can misroute business communication even though it is not usually direct clinical decision support.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace simple telecom-only contact details with the reusable richer ExtendedContactDetail model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated `telecom` while adding `contact`, but that creates duplicate same-resource contact representations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: `ExtendedContactDetail` supports contact purpose, names, addresses, responsible organization, and periods that R4 `telecom` could not carry. A less-breaking transition was possible, but it would put two official contact paths on the same resource for the same business fact. That material duplication tradeoff makes the breaking replacement probably justified, though not fully proven by the supplied artifacts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have retained `OrganizationAffiliation.telecom` as an optional deprecated `ContactPoint` element and added optional `OrganizationAffiliation.contact` for richer details. This would preserve old wire-format instances and clients while enabling the R6 model. The cost is not just migration guidance: validators, serializers, profiles, and business rules would need precedence rules when both paths are populated, and the deprecated representation might persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves most R4 instances, but creates long-lived duplication, precedence ambiguity, and possible inconsistent contact data.

evidence.quote: Official contact details at the participatingOrganization relevant to this Affiliation

evidence.detail: ExtendedContactDetail includes purpose, name, telecom, address, organization, and period, which is a broader content model than ContactPoint.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 fragment is intentionally minimal because `OrganizationAffiliation` has no mandatory local business elements. A practical transform may group multiple R4 telecom repetitions into one R6 contact or create one contact per telecom; that policy is not specified by the base StructureDefinition.

findings.narrativeMd: `OrganizationAffiliation.telecom` is no longer a legal R6 element. The replacement `OrganizationAffiliation.contact` is not merely a rename: its type changes from `ContactPoint` to `ExtendedContactDetail`, so generated classes, serializers, FHIRPath expressions, profile paths, and validation rules must all be updated. R4 data can usually be migrated by nesting each old `ContactPoint` under `contact.telecom`, but rich R6 contact details cannot be flattened back to R4 without losing semantics.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing `telecom` can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6 because R6 has no element at that path. R6 instances using only `contact.telecom` can be partially projected to R4 `telecom`, but any R6 `contact.purpose`, `contact.name`, `contact.address`, `contact.organization`, or `contact.period` needs an extension or will be lost. Strict generated clients will also break at compile time or runtime if they still reference `telecom`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update models and transforms to write `OrganizationAffiliation.contact`. For simple R4 contacts, map `telecom[n]` to either `contact[n].telecom[0]` or to a grouped `contact[0].telecom[n]` according to local semantics. Add fixtures for multiple telecoms, ranked telecoms, contact periods, and rich R6 contact content. For R6→R4, use extensions or a sidecar mapping if contact purpose/name/address/organization/period must survive.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The model change could have been less disruptive by adding `contact` while preserving `telecom` as deprecated for a transition period. That would have allowed old instances and clients to continue working while enabling richer R6 contact detail. The cost would be temporary duplication and a need to define precedence when both elements are present.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No official cross-version StructureMap was available, so grouping policy for R4 telecom repetitions is a migration design decision rather than a computable fact from the supplied inputs.

findings.title: R6 contact forbids telecom and address use='home'

oldState.summary: R4 had no local OrganizationAffiliation rule forbidding ContactPoint.use='home'.

semanticText.definition: Contact details at the participatingOrganization relevant to this Affiliation.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `OrganizationAffiliation.telecom` uses the general `ContactPoint` datatype. The `ContactPointUse` code system includes `home`, and OrganizationAffiliation adds no local constraint excluding it.

newState.summary: R6 adds local error constraints org-3 and org-4 under `OrganizationAffiliation.contact` forbidding `home` use for telecom and address.

constraints.human: The telecom of an organization can never be of use 'home'
The address of an organization can never be of use 'home'

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps `home` as a valid ContactPointUse and AddressUse code generally, but locally prohibits it for OrganizationAffiliation contacts.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A straightforward migration from R4 `telecom` to R6 `contact.telecom` can turn an R4-valid `use='home'` contact into an R6 validation error. The break is conditional because it only affects OrganizationAffiliation contacts using the `home` purpose, and the path replacement itself is covered by the separate contact-model finding.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main risk is incorrect or rejected business contact data. In most OrganizationAffiliation contexts, `home` contact use is likely erroneous, but historical data may contain it.

justification.inferredGoal: Prevent personal home contact semantics from being used for organization affiliation contacts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a warning-level base invariant or best-practice rule before enforcing `home` as a base error.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The policy goal is plausible because OrganizationAffiliation contacts are official organizational contacts, not personal home contact points. The break is conditional and likely rare, but an error-level invariant is the design that actually enforces the base guarantee. A warning would be less disruptive yet materially weaker, so the breaking constraint is probably justified with explicit migration review for historical `home` values.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have made `org-3` and `org-4` warning-level or best-practice constraints, allowing migrated R4 `use='home'` contacts to remain valid while being flagged. That alternative only partially meets the same goal: systems could ignore the warning, and profile-only enforcement would fragment behavior across implementations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Warnings preserve historical data but do not provide the same uniform guarantee that organization contacts are not home contacts.

evidence.detail: R4 OrganizationAffiliation.telecom has no local `home` exclusion; only the inherited ele-1 element constraint appears.
R6 adds an error constraint requiring contact telecom entries not to have `use = 'home'`.
R6 adds an error constraint requiring contact address not to have `use = 'home'`.
The `home` code remains present in the general ContactPointUse and AddressUse code systems in both R4 and R6; the narrowing is local to OrganizationAffiliation.contact.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example changes `use` to `work` only if that is semantically true. If the contact really was a home contact, automatic relabeling would be lossy and should require manual review or an extension-based preservation strategy.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds two local error invariants on `OrganizationAffiliation.contact`: organization affiliation contact telecoms and addresses cannot be marked as `home`. This is a genuine value-domain narrowing for migrated contact data because R4 did not have the same local prohibition on `OrganizationAffiliation.telecom`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 contact point with `use='home'` can be valid in R4. If mapped into R6 as `contact.telecom.use='home'`, it violates `org-3`; a R6 contact address with `use='home'` violates `org-4`. This is not a terminology-code removal, because the general code systems still include `home`; it is a local invariant enforced by R6 validators.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 OrganizationAffiliation telecoms with `use='home'` before migration. Decide whether they are data-quality errors, should be changed to `work`, should drop the use code, or should be preserved in an extension for audit. Do not blindly rewrite `home` to `work` without confirming business meaning.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same policy could have been introduced less disruptively as an implementation-guide rule, a warning invariant, or a staged deprecation. Making it a base error gives stronger consistency but causes migration exceptions for historical R4 data.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because the old path is removed, this finding should be read together with the contact-model replacement finding. It isolates the additional validation failure that remains after a syntactic telecom-to-contact transform.

findings.title: Replacement contact element is no longer included in summary output

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 summary views of OrganizationAffiliation could include affiliation-specific telecom contact details.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 does not mark the replacement `contact` element as a summary element, even though many child fields of `ExtendedContactDetail` are summary within the datatype.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The summary flag comparison follows the same old-to-new contact element match as the main representation-change finding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not make instances invalid, but it can break clients that relied on summary search/read responses or generated summary serializers to include affiliation contact details. Such clients may silently stop receiving contact information in R6 summary-mode interactions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily operational: summary clients may omit directory contact channels unless they request full resources or use search parameters.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly avoid including richer and potentially bulky ExtendedContactDetail content in summary views.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Mark `contact` as summary=true, or retain a summary-capable deprecated `telecom`, but either path has material tradeoffs.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The computable artifacts show the summary-flag break but not the R6 rationale. Avoiding richer `ExtendedContactDetail` content in summary views is a plausible goal, yet the old R4 summary behavior exposed affiliation telecoms and some clients may rely on that. Because the best less-breaking designs have meaningful payload, privacy, or duplication costs, the availability is partial rather than a clean yes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The direct base alternative would set `OrganizationAffiliation.contact` to summary=true so summary-mode responses can still include affiliation contact details. That preserves the old expectation but can pull richer purpose, name, address, organization, and period data into summary responses. A narrower alternative would keep a deprecated summary `telecom` alongside `contact`, but that repeats the duplicate-representation problem from the main contact-model change.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserving summary behavior risks larger or more sensitive summary payloads, or else duplicates contact data across old and new paths.

examples.examplesMd: A R4 `_summary=true` response could include `telecom`; a comparable R6 summary response is not expected to include `contact` based on the element summary flag.

findings.narrativeMd: The contact replacement also changes summary behavior. In R4, `telecom` was a summary element. In R6, the replacement `contact` is not. That can surprise clients that use summary-mode responses for provider-directory listings and expect contact channels to be present.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an instance-validity break. It is a serialization/API behavior risk: full R6 resources can contain `contact`, but summary views may omit it. Generated summary serializers and clients that use `_summary=true` need to be retested.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Clients that need affiliation contact data should request full resources, verify R6 SearchParameter behavior, or explicitly include contact data through supported server mechanisms. Regression tests should compare full and summary responses before and after migration.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The less disruptive choice would have been to keep the replacement contact element in the summary set. If the concern was payload size or sensitivity, narrower guidance or server-level controls could have been used instead of a base summary flag change.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The package compose contains the same 117 SNOMED codes in R4 and R6; four display labels changed. Because the binding is weakened to example, these display changes do not create a base validation failure.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 treats the same value set as examples only. Validators and authoring tools should no longer treat the value set as the preferred source for this element unless a profile says otherwise.

facts.note: Code membership unchanged in package compose; four display labels changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Weakening a binding from preferred to example is not a validation break; it reduces conformance pressure. The risk is behavioral: validators, UI pickers, analytics, or profile authors that assumed C80 practice codes were the preferred base vocabulary may need to adjust expectations.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Specialty coding affects directory classification and matching. The base change is permissive, but looser vocabulary guidance can reduce interoperability if profiles do not constrain it.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow broader specialty coding than the C80 practice setting value set implies.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No backward-compatible alternative is needed because weakening a preferred binding to example does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of allowing broader specialty coding is reasonable, and the change is not a hard R4-to-R6 instance break: both preferred and example bindings permit codes outside the value set in base validation. The main cost is weaker interoperability guidance, which implementers can address with profiles when C80/SNOMED specialty coding is required.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Backward-compatible alternative analysis is not applicable here because the R6 base design is already permissive for existing R4 data. Keeping the R4 preferred binding would be a different interoperability signal, not a less-breaking base design needed to preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining the preferred binding would preserve stronger vocabulary convergence but would be a conformance-policy choice, not a compatibility-preserving alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is preferred to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/c80-practice-codes`.
R6 binding strength is example to the same canonical value set.
The packaged R4 and R6 compose definitions both list 117 SNOMED codes; four display labels changed and no code membership change was detected in the package files.

examples.examplesMd: No old-valid/new-invalid instance example applies because both preferred and example bindings allow codes outside the value set in base FHIR validation.

findings.narrativeMd: The `specialty` binding is weaker in R6. This is not instance-breaking, but it changes the conformance signal: C80 practice codes move from the vocabulary implementers are encouraged to use to a set of examples. Systems that generate pick lists, warnings, or data-quality metrics from binding strength should revisit this element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with any `CodeableConcept` remains structurally representable in R6, and an R6 instance remains structurally representable in R4. The practical difference is validator and tooling behavior: R4 preferred bindings may produce guidance or warnings where R6 example bindings generally should not.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review specialty validation, UI pick lists, and analytics rules. If a deployment still requires C80/SNOMED specialty coding, capture that requirement in a profile rather than relying on the R6 base binding.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is backward-compatible for instances but not for conformance expectations. If the goal was flexibility, a profile-based approach could have preserved a stronger base recommendation while allowing local overrides.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The element type, cardinality, and target profile did not change, so there is no structural validation break. The risk is semantic: R6 data may use `network` for non-insurance networks that are syntactically representable in R4 but may be interpreted by R4 systems as health insurance provider networks.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misclassification of network semantics can affect directory filtering or payer/network business logic.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize network participation beyond insurance-specific provider networks.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No backward-compatible alternative is needed because the element shape and targets are unchanged and R4 instances remain valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing `network` beyond health-insurance provider networks is a plausible R6 goal, and it was accomplished without changing cardinality, type, or reference target. The remaining risk is semantic interpretation of newer R6 uses by R4-era systems, not an R4-to-R6 validation break. On that basis the change is probably justified and the backward-compatible alternative question is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A conservative design could have kept the R4 insurance-specific wording and handled non-insurance networks through profiles or documentation, but that would not be a backward-compatible base alternative needed to preserve R4-valid instances. It would mainly preserve an older, narrower interpretation at the cost of the R6 generalization.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping insurance-specific wording would protect older assumptions but would leave the base model less reusable for non-insurance networks.

evidence.detail: R4 definition begins with "Health insurance provider network".
R6 definition says "The network" and adds a comment that health insurance provider networks are a common example.

examples.examplesMd: The example is syntactically representable in R4 because the reference target is still Organization, but it may not be semantically clean if an R4 consumer assumes the target is a health insurance provider network.

findings.narrativeMd: `OrganizationAffiliation.network` did not change shape, but its definition broadened. R4 described it as a health insurance provider network; R6 describes a network generally and mentions health insurance as a common example. This is a semantic compatibility risk for systems with payer-network-specific assumptions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No base validator will reject an instance because of this wording change. The compatibility issue is interpretation: a valid R6 non-insurance network reference can be carried in R4 syntax but may be misleading to R4-era applications or profiles that encoded the old insurance-network assumption.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review business rules, search filters, and UI labels that assume `network` means insurance network. If projecting R6 data to R4 consumers, consider profile metadata, extensions, or documentation to distinguish non-insurance network affiliations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is structurally backward-compatible. A stricter backward-compatible approach would have kept the old wording and used profiles for broader networks, but that would preserve an insurance-centric base model.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id/name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. R6 status/maturity metadata changed, but no identity rename, split, merge, or removal was detected.

`organization`, `participatingOrganization`, `network`, `location`, `healthcareService`, and `endpoint` retain the same reference target profiles.

No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limits were found.
No local OrganizationAffiliation business element changed to or from `isModifier=true`. Inherited base modifier behavior is out of scope.
No local slicing definitions were found for OrganizationAffiliation elements in either version.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Resource maturity/status metadata advanced
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 keeps the same resource identity and content model while changing artifact metadata from draft/trial-use/FMM 0 to active/normative/FMM 1. This does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance, documentation, or code-generation pipelines that filter on standards status or FMM may treat the R6 artifact differently.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Directional relationship comments added for organization and participatingOrganization
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The cardinality, type, and definitions are unchanged; R6 adds explanatory comments and examples clarifying the direction between `organization` and `participatingOrganization`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that treated affiliations as symmetric should review whether they should model joint partnerships as a third Organization with two OrganizationAffiliations, as suggested by the R6 comment.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records mustSupport=false on local elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 generally omits `mustSupport`; R6 explicitly sets `mustSupport:false` on local elements. This is equivalent for base conformance and does not make instances invalid.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that distinguishes absent from false should normalize the values before reporting false-positive changes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `OrganizationAffiliation.contact` depends on the R6 `ExtendedContactDetail` datatype. A dedicated datatype analysis should assess its own R4/R6 compatibility and codegen impact.
Inherited base-resource changes appear in the snapshots but are intentionally excluded from this local report. They should be handled by base artifact reports.

Package indexes show OrganizationAffiliation search parameters in both releases, including telecom-related search parameters despite the local element replacement. Search behavior needs separate SearchParameter analysis.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 differential narrative or ballot change log was used. Structural conclusions are reliable, but intent and justification are inferred from the artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official release notes, Jira tickets, or generated version-comparison pages for OrganizationAffiliation.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official ConceptMap or StructureMap was available for transforming R4 `telecom` to R6 `contact`, so grouping and lossless-preservation guidance is inferred rather than authoritative.
